speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing difficulties conceiving and discomfort during sexual activity. To better understand your situation, have these symptoms been present for more than a year?

speaker: Patient
text: 30-year-old female. The patient and her husband have been trying to conceive for 15 months without success. They are sexually active at least twice a week. The husband occasionally has difficulties maintaining an erection. The patient reports discomfort and pelvic floor muscle tension during attempted vaginal penetration. Diagnosed with body dysmorphic disorder three years ago. No family history of serious illness. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. No medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your history of pelvic floor muscle tension and body dysmorphic disorder, have you experienced any pain specifically during ovulation or intercourse that you describe as "deep" or "sharp," and have you noticed any abnormal vaginal discharge or bleeding?

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Vulvodynia / Vaginismus secondary to Body Dysmorphic Disorder and Pelvic Floor Dysfunction.

The clinical picture of 15 months of infertility combined with pain specifically during penetration, deep pelvic floor tension, and a history of Body Dysmorphic Disorder is highly characteristic of this diagnosis. The husband's erectile difficulties and lack of systemic risk factors support a primary gynecological/psychogenic etiology rather than a systemic infection or malignancy. No further tests are required to confirm this clinical diagnosis; management will involve pelvic floor physical therapy and psychiatric referral for the underlying disorder.
